name: Anise
grown_as: An annual herb grown for its aniseed-flavoured seed. Rare in UK gardens; it needs a long warm summer to ripen seed.
habit: A slender branched annual 30 to 60 cm tall, with a round grooved stem finely downy all over. The leaves change shape from the base to the top.

leaf.arrangement: Basal leaves in a small rosette; stem leaves alternate
leaf.type: Three kinds up the plant. Basal leaves simple and undivided. Middle leaves pinnate with three to five leaflets. Upper leaves two or three times pinnate, with narrow line-like segments.
leaf.outline: Basal leaves round to kidney-shaped, 2 to 5 cm; middle leaflets wedge- to fan-shaped; upper segments thread-like
leaf.base: Basal leaves heart-shaped at the base
leaf.tip: Rounded on basal leaves; pointed on upper segments
leaf.margin: Basal leaves coarsely toothed and shallowly lobed all round; middle leaflets toothed on the outer edge
leaf.veins: Palmate on basal leaves, not prominent
leaf.stalk: Basal leaves on long stalks; upper leaves on short sheathing bases

flower.petals: Five tiny white petals per flower, notched with an inturned tip
flower.behind: No bracts or one; bracteoles one or none
flower.carried: At the ends of stems and branches, facing up, on 7 to 15 slender downy rays

fruit: Egg-shaped seeds 3 to 5 mm, slightly flattened, with fine ribs and short close hairs, greyish-brown with a greenish tint
seedling: Two narrow oval seed leaves, then first true leaves round and toothed

leaf: a basal leaf rounded to kidney-shaped and coarsely toothed
upper leaves finely cut, so the change of shape up the stem shows
seed: small egg-shaped ribbed seed, downy, greyish-brown
seedling: first true leaf rounded and toothed
young: rounded toothed basal leaves on long stalks
first finely cut leaves on the rising stem
flower: rounded lower leaves and feathery upper ones
seedhead: umbels of small grey-brown egg-shaped seeds

look_alikes: Burnet-saxifrage (Pimpinella saxifraga), a wild perennial, has pinnate basal leaves. Coriander has hairless leaves and round seeds. Star anise is an unrelated tree spice.
